correctness.rationale: The threshold projection is invariant under common translation. Its active-set derivative J_F subtracts the active mean on F and vanishes elsewhere; each F occurs on a strict open cell. Segment integration gives the maximum of the local norms, and a one-jump step attains each local norm because the path-difference map identifies the quotient by constants with an l1 space. At a cut with a,b active positions on the two sides, the output is −b/(a+b) and a/(a+b) on those respective positions. The middle edge splits additively by sign. Appending a zero toward the cut on each side gives max transition count min(2a,2z+1) on a side with a ones and z zeros, attained by alternating runs. In the deficit formula, for a=b each side deficit is nonnegative and vanishes only for u,v in {−1,0}; this gives n=4a−2,4a−1,4a. If b>a and b≤3a, the minimum v-term is at v=−1 (possibly tied when b=3a) and the integer numerator of the deficit is at least d(2d−1) for d=b−a. Equality at one requires d=1,u=0,v=−1, hence n=2(a+b)−1; if b>3a the integer numerator is at least b²−ab+2a(a−1)>1. All larger numerators give a deficit at least 1/(a+b)>1/(n+1). The residue-specific selectors realize the claimed maxima, including n=2. Strict slack gives distinct arbitrarily close attaining inputs, and scalar clipping gives only the separate one-input variation bound. Positive mass scales out. Independent exact replay in branches/db9cfbef-f580-405f-ba1d-713faf127430/independent_check.py checked 851,867 active-support/cut cases through n=15, 72 boundary counts, and all integer maxima and strict witnesses through n=100. The universal result is analytical, not an extrapolation.
